- [ ] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

## Problem

`GTPWeightCache` pins one buffer per cache key (shape, dtype, direction, chain) for the whole
run. On an Ultra rank at GTP 64 that is 217 buffers, 17 GB, although only the current layer, the
prefetched next layer and a little scratch are ever in flight: about 1 GB during the backward and
1.2 GB between steps. The forward buffers sit idle through the whole backward and optimizer step,
the backward buffers through the whole forward.

## What this PR does

Eager (non-CUDA-graph) chains stop pinning their buffers. CUDA-graph chains keep the pooled
buffers with fixed addresses, since replay needs them. No new command-line option: the new
policy is the default, it falls back by itself where the assumptions do not hold, and
`GTP_CONFIG.eager_buffer_policy` (`"slab"` | `"transient"` | `"pooled"`) remains an internal
knob for tests and diagnosis.

**Transient buffers (the warm-up and the fallback).** `acquire(ticket, producer_stream)`
allocates the buffer when the collective is issued and the buffer is freed once its consumer
has been enqueued. Because the consumer is enqueued only after the call that returned the
buffer (and the next layer's prefetch is issued from inside that call), `consume` tags the
buffer with a *consume epoch* (`begin_consume` bumps it at the top of every call that hands
gathered weights to a consumer) and the buffer is freed at the first `acquire` of a later
epoch. Reduce-scatter outputs are freed by `release` right after `main_grad.add_`. The wgrad
GEMM output and FP32-RS all-to-all scratch follow the same rule and record the reduce-scatter
stream before they are dropped. The writing collective waits on an event of the allocating
stream; a reader on another stream is recorded on the buffer.

**The weight slab (steady state).** A training step's schedule is static, so step 2 runs
transient while every acquire and free is recorded (step 1 is skipped: its prefetch links are
still forming); at its boundary the recorded lifetimes are packed largest-first into one slab
(each region at the lowest offset clear of every region live at the same time; a time-bucket
index keeps the plan at about a second for 22k regions) and from step 3 each (ticket, n-th
acquire of the step) reuses its fixed slice, MXFP8 tensors built once over the slice. The
steady-state path is a position lookup: the k-th acquire of a step binds the k-th recorded
region, and the plan holds for every region the regions that last used each of its bytes, so
the writer waits only on those (the previous reader when it ran on another stream, the previous
writer when nobody read it). No per-step allocation, no `record_stream`, no per-acquire search;
the one-GPU micro-benchmark puts the whole acquire/consume/free round trip at about 6 µs against
1.5 µs for the pooled lookup, which is 0.1 s per step at 22k acquires.

**Keeping the run's peak in the steady state.** Three details decide whether the recording
phase, not the steady state, sets the run's peak. Consumed buffers are freed at the step
boundary, where every consumer is enqueued, instead of at the next step's first acquire. The
cache is released once before the recording step and once before the slab is allocated, so the
optimizer state, the recording and the slab start from a compact pool. And the largest buffers
(the vocabulary tables, 5 GB each) get fixed slices only if the optimizer step is not the run's
peak, read from the rise of the maximum allocated through the optimizer step before the
recording: at a forward/backward peak the table gathers are live, so their slices cost nothing
and end the per-step churn of the largest buffers; when the optimizer step is the peak (Muon at
small data parallelism) no gather is live there, and the tables stay transient.

**Where the assumptions do not hold.** The first acquire that leaves the recorded order (a
skipped prefetch, a replayed layer) ends the slab for that step: the rest of the step runs on
transient buffers and the step boundary fences every stream that touched the slab; the counts
appear in the memory report (`gtp buffers: slab ... conflicts N, misses M`). Two such steps in
a row mean the schedule changed (a batch-size ramp, for example): the plan and the slab are
dropped and re-recorded from the next two steps; after three failed plans the run stays
transient. Evaluation passes are bracketed by `set_forward_only` and run on transient buffers
without touching the plan. `finalize_model_grads` calls `step_boundary()` once per step.

## Results (same running config in every phase, same ranks, main's unconditional code otherwise)

This PR alone on top of main, same running config, same ranks.

64 GPUs, production shapes (GTP 64 / EP 8 / EGTP 8, 164 layers, 4 micro-batches, Muon, mock data
with real routing, 16 steps, job 1400953). Main is a pristine checkout of 3e66acdb6 built in its own
worktree. Steady = max over ranks and steps 6 to 15; the run's peak is the steady state (step 1
207 GiB, the recording step 230 GiB).

| phase | step time | steady allocated | steady reserved | device memory |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | 33.6 s | 213.1 GiB | 254.6 GiB | 275.7 GiB |
| PR (default) | 33.65 s (+0.1%) | 197.3 GiB (-15.8) | 238.5 GiB (-16.1) | 259.6 GiB (-16.1) |

Reserved at this scale varies by about +-7 GiB between runs of identical code (two runs of the same
PR tree measured 227.8 and 241.6 GiB on identical allocated); allocated is the stable signal. Plan:
21,972 regions in a 4.7 GB slab, zero conflicts or misses, the three vocabulary-table tickets
transient; one acquire costs ~6 us of host time (pooled lookup 1.4 us).

16 GPUs, reduced layout (GTP 16 / EP 2 / EGTP 8, mock data with real routing, Adam, 1 micro-batch,
16 steps, job 1400952):

| phase | step time | steady allocated | steady reserved | device memory |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main (pooled) | 1.26 s | 89.8 GiB | 104.7 GiB | 118.5 GiB |
| PR (default) | 1.26 s | 82.9 GiB (-6.9) | 101.3 GiB (-3.5) | 115.0 GiB (-3.5) |

With `weight_slab_max_bytes=None` (the tables pinned) the 16-GPU steady reserved was 98.3 GiB in
three runs; at 64 GPUs the same setting cost 7 GiB of allocated, so the default keeps the tables
transient. Stacked with the offload-stream PR the savings add (16 GPUs -5.3 GiB, 64 GPUs -18 GiB).

256 GPUs, EP 64 house layout (GTP 64 / EP 64 / EGTP 4, 82 layers, 1 micro-batch, global batch 256,
Adam, mock data with forced balancing, nsys on rank 0, 16 steps, job 1360166), main and PR twice each,
interleaved on the same ranks; numbers are the mean of the two phases, steady = steps 6 to 15:
| phase | step time (mean / median) | steady allocated | steady reserved | resident | device memory at peak |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | 3.224 / 3.226 s | 166.9 GiB | 185.7 GiB | 128.8 GiB | 206.9 GiB |
| PR, default (slab) | 3.240 / 3.233 s (+0.5% / +0.2%) | 160.3 GiB (-6.7, -4.0%) | 180.3 GiB (-5.4, -2.9%) | 112.1 GiB (-16.8) | 201.4 GiB (-5.6, -2.7%) |

(These 256-GPU numbers are from an earlier tree of this PR with two recording steps; the final
tree's 256-GPU run is pending and will replace them.) The two main phases differ by 0.9% in step
time, so the PR's +0.5% is inside the spread. The plan is
2,699 regions in a 4.5 GB slab (3.9 GB live at the peak), zero conflicts or misses. The reserved
saving is smaller than at 64 GPUs: with one micro-batch per step the pinned cache is smaller to begin
with, and the two 5 GB vocabulary-table gathers (above `weight_slab_max_bytes`, transient) and the
activations reuse the memory the slab frees. Resident memory, the part held between steps, drops
16.8 GiB at both scales.

# Issues

#6609 

## Contribution process

### Pre-checks

- [ ] I have added relevant unit tests
- [ ] I have added relevant functional tests
- [ ] If this PR adds or changes a GPU kernel (Triton, `jit_fuser`/`torch.compile`, CUDA extension, TE or external-library dispatch, or a scatter/index accumulation), I have added or updated its bit-exact determinism test and registered it in `tests/unit_tests/determinism/kernels/manifest.py` ([guide](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/main/docs/developer/determinism/testing.md))
- [ ] I have added proper typing to my code [Typing guidelines](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html)
- [ ] I have added relevant documentation
- [ ] I have run the [autoformatter.sh](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/main/tools/autoformat.sh) on my PR

+    step 2 on. Per step: ``a`` then ``b`` consumed in successive epochs (so b's acquire frees
+    a), ``c`` prefetched while b is live and consumed last, a reduce-scatter output released
+    after its add. c is still pending at the boundary; the recording step's boundary frees it
+    before planning, later steps leave it to the next step's first acquire.
+    """

+    def setup_method(self):
+        gtp_module.update_gtp_config(eager_buffer_policy="slab", weight_slab_plan_step=1)
+        self.cache = GTPWeightCache()
+        self.producer = torch.cuda.Stream()
+        cache = self.cache
+        self.a = cache.reserve(_StubParam(64, 32), torch.bfloat16, fwd=True)
+        self.b = cache.reserve(_StubParam(64, 32), torch.bfloat16, fwd=True)
+        self.c = cache.reserve(_StubParam(128, 32), torch.bfloat16, fwd=False)
+        self.rs = cache.reserve(_StubParam(64, 32), torch.float32, fwd=False, reduce_scatter=True)

+    def teardown_method(self):
+        self.cache.clear()
+        gtp_module.update_gtp_config(

+        )
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()

+    def _step(self, skip_c=False):
+        cache, producer = self.cache, self.producer
+        cache.begin_consume()
+        cache.acquire(self.a, producer)
+        cache.consume(self.a)
+        cache.begin_consume()
+        cache.acquire(self.b, producer)
+        if not skip_c:
+            cache.acquire(self.c, producer)
+        cache.consume(self.b)
+        cache.begin_consume()
+        if not skip_c:
+            cache.consume(self.c)
+        cache.acquire(self.rs, producer)
+        cache.release(self.rs)
+        cache.step_boundary()

+    def test_plan_packs_disjoint_lifetimes_into_shared_bytes(self):
+        cache = self.cache
+        self._step()  # the recorded step: the plan is built at its boundary
+        plan = cache._plan
+        assert plan is not None and cache._slab_disabled is None
+        a, b, c, rs = (plan[(t, 0)] for t in (self.a, self.b, self.c, self.rs))
+        assert (a.nbytes, b.nbytes, c.nbytes, rs.nbytes) == (4096, 4096, 8192, 4096)
+        # Largest first: c (live until the step boundary) takes offset 0; a never overlaps c
+        # in time and shares its bytes; b and the reduce-scatter output overlap c and go above
+        # it, the output reusing b's offset since b is freed before it.
+        assert c.offset == 0 and len(c.arc) == 1  # consumed last: freed at the step boundary
+        assert a.offset == 0 and b.offset == 8192 and rs.offset == 8192
+        assert cache.slab_bytes == 2 << 20  # rounded like a large allocation
+        assert cache.slab_lower_bound == 8192 + 4096  # b and c live at once
+        # Predecessors: who last used each byte before the acquire. a's bytes were c's; c's
+        # bytes were a's (first half) and its own (second half); rs reuses b's offset.
+        assert set(a.preds) == {c} and set(c.preds) == {a, c} and set(rs.preds) == {b}

+def _build_stack(world_size, dtype, recipe):
+    from tests.unit_tests.generalized_tensor_parallel.test_gtp_basics import (
+        _make_native_fp8_gtp_linear,
+    )
+
+    gtp_remat_group = dist.new_group(list(range(world_size)))
+    if recipe is None:
+
+        def make(in_f, out_f):
+            return _make_gtp_linear(
+                in_f, out_f, gtp_remat_group, dtype, fuse_wgrad_accumulation=True
+            )
+
+    else:
+
+        def make(in_f, out_f):
+            return _make_native_fp8_gtp_linear(in_f, out_f, gtp_remat_group, dtype, recipe)
+
+    recomputed = [make(HIDDEN, HIDDEN) for _ in range(NUM_LAYERS)]
+    spacers = [(make(HIDDEN, OTHER), make(OTHER, HIDDEN)) for _ in range(NUM_LAYERS)]
+    layers = recomputed + [module for pair in spacers for module in pair]
+    for layer in layers:
+        layer.weight.main_grad = torch.zeros(layer.weight.shape, dtype=dtype, device="cuda")
+    return recomputed, spacers, layers

+
+def _step(recomputed, spacers, x, recompute, recipe):
+    from transformer_engine.pytorch import fp8_autocast
+
+    context = fp8_autocast(enabled=True, fp8_recipe=recipe) if recipe is not None else nullcontext()
+    with context:
+        h = x
+        for layer, (down, up) in zip(recomputed, spacers):
+            if recompute:
+                checkpoint = CheckpointWithoutOutput()
+                y = checkpoint.checkpoint(lambda inp, l=layer: l(inp), h)
+                h = torch.nn.functional.gelu(y)
+                checkpoint.discard_output_and_register_recompute(h)
+            else:
+                h = torch.nn.functional.gelu(layer(h))
+            h = torch.nn.functional.gelu(down(h))
+            h = torch.nn.functional.gelu(up(h))
+    loss = h.float().sum()
+    loss.backward()
+    return x.grad.detach().clone()
+
+
+def _run_variant(world_size, dtype, recipe, transient, recompute, iterations=4, slab=False):
+    """Fresh chains and cache; returns per-iteration (dgrad, wgrads...), pooled bytes, the
+    transient peak and the per-iteration allocator peaks. ``slab``: plan from steps 2-3."""
+    gtp_module.reset_gtp_state()
+    gtp_module._GTP_CACHE = None
+    policy = "slab" if slab else ("transient" if transient else "pooled")
+    gtp_module.update_gtp_config(eager_buffer_policy=policy, weight_slab_plan_step=2)
+    try:
+        torch.manual_seed(0)
+        recomputed, spacers, layers = _build_stack(world_size, dtype, recipe)
+        torch.manual_seed(1)
+        x = torch.randn(BATCH, HIDDEN, dtype=dtype, device="cuda", requires_grad=True)
+        dist.broadcast(x, src=0)
+        results, peaks = [], []
+        for _ in range(iterations):
+            for layer in layers:
+                layer.weight.main_grad.zero_()
+            x.grad = None
+            torch.cuda.synchronize()
+            torch.cuda.reset_peak_memory_stats()
+            dgrad = _step(recomputed, spacers, x, recompute, recipe)
+            gtp_module.get_global_GTP_cache().step_boundary()
+            results.append([dgrad] + [layer.weight.main_grad.clone() for layer in layers])
+            torch.cuda.synchronize()
+            peaks.append(torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated())
+        cache = gtp_module.get_global_GTP_cache()
+        if slab:
+            assert cache._slab is not None and cache._plan, cache._slab_disabled
+            assert cache.slab_conflicts == 0 and cache.slab_misses == 0, (
+                cache.slab_conflicts,
+                cache.slab_misses,
+            )
+            assert 0 < cache.peak_slab_live_bytes <= cache.slab_bytes
+            assert cache.slab_lower_bound <= cache.slab_bytes
+        if transient:
+            transient_slots = [slot for slot in cache._slots.values() if slot.transient]
+            assert transient_slots, "no transient tickets"
+            # Nothing is pooled for transient tickets, and only the buffers consumed in the last
+            # epoch (plus a prefetch) may still be bound, never one per ticket.
+            assert not any(cache._pool.get(slot.key) for slot in transient_slots), "pooled"
+            bound = sum(1 for slot in transient_slots if slot.buf is not None)
+            assert bound <= max(3, len(transient_slots) // 3), (bound, len(transient_slots))
+        return results, cache._total_bytes, cache.peak_transient_bytes, peaks
+    finally:
+        gtp_module.update_gtp_config(eager_buffer_policy="slab")
+        gtp_module.reset_gtp_state()
+        gtp_module._GTP_CACHE = None
+
+
+def _worker_slab_matches_pooled_cache(rank, world_size, port, recompute, use_mxfp8):
+    dtype = torch.bfloat16
+    recipe = None
+    if use_mxfp8:
+        from transformer_engine.common.recipe import MXFP8BlockScaling
+
+        recipe = MXFP8BlockScaling()
+    reference, _, _, _ = _run_variant(world_size, dtype, recipe, False, recompute, iterations=6)
+    candidate, _, _, _ = _run_variant(
+        world_size, dtype, recipe, True, recompute, iterations=6, slab=True
+    )
+    for iteration, (ref_values, values) in enumerate(zip(reference, candidate)):
+        for index, (ref, value) in enumerate(zip(ref_values, values)):
+            torch.testing.assert_close(
+                value.float(),
+                ref.float(),
+                rtol=1e-3,
+                atol=1e-3,
+                msg=f"iteration {iteration}, tensor {index} differs with the weight slab",
+            )
+
+
+def _worker_transient_matches_pooled_cache(rank, world_size, port, recompute, use_mxfp8):
+    dtype = torch.bfloat16
+    recipe = None
+    if use_mxfp8:
+        from transformer_engine.common.recipe import MXFP8BlockScaling
+
+        recipe = MXFP8BlockScaling()
+    reference, pooled_bytes, _, _ = _run_variant(world_size, dtype, recipe, False, recompute)
+    candidate, _, transient_peak, peaks = _run_variant(world_size, dtype, recipe, True, recompute)
+    for iteration, (ref_values, values) in enumerate(zip(reference, candidate)):
+        for index, (ref, value) in enumerate(zip(ref_values, values)):
+            torch.testing.assert_close(
+                value.float(),
+                ref.float(),
+                rtol=1e-3,
+                atol=1e-3,
+                msg=f"iteration {iteration}, tensor {index} differs with transient buffers",
+            )
+    assert pooled_bytes > 0 and transient_peak > 0
+    # No warm-up, nothing pinned: the first iteration never exceeds the steady state beyond the
+    # allocator's rounding slack.
+    assert peaks[0] <= max(peaks[1:]) + (4 << 20), peaks
+
+
+def _reset_scratch_state():
+    gtp_module.reset_gtp_state()
+    gtp_module._GTP_CACHE = None
+    gtp_module._wgrad_buf_pool.clear()
+
+
+def _run_scratch_variant(world_size, dtype, transient, fp32_rs, symm, iterations=5):
+    """Fresh state; returns per-iteration main_grads and whether the recycled scratch pool
+    stayed empty."""
+    from megatron.core.tensor_parallel import gtp_symmetric_memory as gtp_symm
+
+    _reset_scratch_state()
+    gtp_module.update_gtp_config(
+        eager_buffer_policy="transient" if transient else "pooled",
+        reduce_scatter_with_fp32_accumulation=fp32_rs,
+    )
+    gtp_remat_group = dist.new_group(list(range(world_size)))
+    if symm:
+        gtp_symm.register_gtp_symm_pool(gtp_remat_group)
+    try:
+        torch.manual_seed(0)
+        layers = [
+            _make_gtp_linear(HIDDEN, HIDDEN, gtp_remat_group, dtype, fuse_wgrad_accumulation=True),
+            _make_gtp_linear(HIDDEN, OTHER, gtp_remat_group, dtype, fuse_wgrad_accumulation=True),
+            _make_gtp_linear(OTHER, HIDDEN, gtp_remat_group, dtype, fuse_wgrad_accumulation=True),
+        ]
+        for layer in layers:
+            layer.weight.main_grad = torch.zeros(layer.weight.shape, dtype=dtype, device="cuda")
+        torch.manual_seed(1)
+        x = torch.randn(BATCH, HIDDEN, dtype=dtype, device="cuda", requires_grad=True)
+        dist.broadcast(x, src=0)
+        results = []
+        for _ in range(iterations):
+            for layer in layers:
+                layer.weight.main_grad.zero_()
+            x.grad = None
+            h = x
+            for layer in layers:
+                h = torch.nn.functional.gelu(layer(h))
+            h.float().sum().backward()
+            results.append([x.grad.clone()] + [layer.weight.main_grad.clone() for layer in layers])
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+        pool_empty = not any(gtp_module._wgrad_buf_pool.values())
+        return results, pool_empty
+    finally:
+        del layers
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+        if symm:
+            gtp_symm.deregister_and_clear_gtp_symm_pools()
+        gtp_module.update_gtp_config(
+            eager_buffer_policy="slab", reduce_scatter_with_fp32_accumulation=False
+        )
+        _reset_scratch_state()
+
+
+def _worker_transient_scratch_matches_pools(rank, world_size, port, fp32_rs, symm):
+    from megatron.core.tensor_parallel import gtp_symmetric_memory as gtp_symm
+
+    dtype = torch.bfloat16
+    if symm:
+        group = dist.new_group(list(range(world_size)))
+        try:
+            gtp_symm.register_gtp_symm_pool(group)
+        except Exception as exc:  # NCCL window registration unavailable here
+            pytest.skip(f"NCCL symmetric registration unavailable: {exc}")
+        gtp_symm.deregister_and_clear_gtp_symm_pools()
+    reference, _ = _run_scratch_variant(world_size, dtype, False, fp32_rs, symm)
+    candidate, pool_empty = _run_scratch_variant(world_size, dtype, True, fp32_rs, symm)
+    for iteration, (ref_values, values) in enumerate(zip(reference, candidate)):
+        for index, (ref, value) in enumerate(zip(ref_values, values)):
+            torch.testing.assert_close(
+                value.float(),
+                ref.float(),
+                rtol=1e-3,
+                atol=1e-3,
+                msg=f"iteration {iteration}, tensor {index} differs with transient scratch",
+            )
+    assert pool_empty, "transient scratch was recycled into the per-shape pool"
+
+
+class TestGTPTransientScratchParity:
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize("fp32_rs", [False, True], ids=["rs", "fp32rs"])
+    def test_plain_scratch_matches_pools(self, fp32_rs):
+        _requires_multi_gpu(4)
+        _run_distributed(_worker_transient_scratch_matches_pools, 4, fp32_rs, False)
+
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize("fp32_rs", [False, True], ids=["rs", "fp32rs"])
+    def test_registered_send_path_matches_pools(self, fp32_rs):
+        _requires_multi_gpu(4)
+        _run_distributed(_worker_transient_scratch_matches_pools, 4, fp32_rs, True)
+
+
+class TestGTPTransientBufferParity:
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize("recompute", [False, True], ids=["plain", "recompute"])
+    def test_bf16_matches_pooled_cache(self, recompute):
+        _requires_multi_gpu(4)
+        _run_distributed(_worker_transient_matches_pooled_cache, 4, recompute, False)
+
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize("recompute", [False, True], ids=["plain", "recompute"])
+    def test_mxfp8_matches_pooled_cache(self, recompute):
+        _requires_mxfp8()
+        _requires_multi_gpu(4)
+        _run_distributed(_worker_transient_matches_pooled_cache, 4, recompute, True)
+
+
+class TestGTPWeightSlabParity:
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize("recompute", [False, True], ids=["plain", "recompute"])
+    def test_bf16_slab_matches_pooled_cache(self, recompute):
+        _requires_multi_gpu(4)
+        _run_distributed(_worker_slab_matches_pooled_cache, 4, recompute, False)
+
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize("recompute", [False, True], ids=["plain", "recompute"])
+    def test_mxfp8_slab_matches_pooled_cache(self, recompute):
+        _requires_mxfp8()
+        _requires_multi_gpu(4)
+        _run_distributed(_worker_slab_matches_pooled_cache, 4, recompute, True)
